summary.headline: A holding company at a discount to its parts, but the parts earn less than their cost of capital: fair value about Rs 60.50
summary.text: Vallibel One PLC (VONE.N0000) holds 51.75% of LB Finance, 55.96% of Royal Ceramics, 14.95% of Sampath Bank, 68.75% of Delmege, the unfinished Greener Water hotel and, since October, just over half of The Fortress Resorts; the holding company itself has no debt. Year to March 2026: revenue Rs 149.3bn (+22%), profit to owners Rs 13.17bn (+12%), EPS Rs 11.57, dividend Rs 3.00. The first half of this year was better again: EPS Rs 4.93 against Rs 4.03 (+22%), led by LB Finance after its purchase of Associated Motor Finance. At Rs 88.80 (CSE close on 30 September 2026; the current price couldn't be fetched) the share is 7.1x trailing EPS of Rs 12.47 and 0.81x NAV of Rs 110.29, and about 15% below what its stakes are worth at today's market prices (about Rs 104 a share). But owners' ROE has been only 10–12.5% for three years against an 18.3% cost of equity (beta 0.98), and Royal Ceramics, a quarter of the value, is itself valued by this site at well below its price. On four methods (sum of the parts, P/E, justified P/B, residual income) the fair value is about Rs 60.50, so the price is about 47% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 51.40 and treat under Rs 45.40 as a strong buy. It passes 2 of the 4 business tests (debt and steady profit; it fails on returns and cash), so it goes in category 3, avoid for now.

quality.reason: No debt at the holding company and ten years of profit, but owners' ROE of 10–12.5% and little of the group's profit reaching shareholders as cash. First assessment, 16 November 2026.

fullText:
**Summary**

Vallibel One PLC (VONE.N0000) is Mr Dhammika Perera's holding company. Its value sits in three listed stakes and a handful of private businesses: 51.75% of LB Finance (the biggest piece, about 41% of the parts at market prices), 55.96% of Royal Ceramics (tiles, bathware, and a further 26.08% of LB Finance), 14.95% of Sampath Bank, 68.75% of Delmege (consumer and trading), 100% of Greener Water (an unfinished hotel project) and, since October 2026, just over half of The Fortress Resorts. The holding company itself has no debt and about Rs 3.9bn of cash and deposits.

Results are strong and rising. Year to March 2026: revenue Rs 149.3bn (+22%), profit to owners Rs 13.17bn (+12%), EPS Rs 11.57, dividend Rs 3.00. Six months to September 2026: EPS Rs 4.93 against Rs 4.03 (+22%), driven by LB Finance (segment profit +27%) after it bought Associated Motor Finance. NAV is Rs 110.29.

At Rs 88.80 (CSE close at 30 September 2026, from the interim report; the current CSE price wasn't reachable from this run) the share is 7.1x trailing EPS of Rs 12.47 and 0.81x NAV. That looks cheap, and it is about 15% below what the parts are worth at today's market prices (about Rs 104 a share). But the group earns only about 11–12% on owners' equity, well under the 18.3% a shareholder should demand at a beta of 0.98, and two of the three listed stakes (Royal Ceramics and, at the bull end, Sampath) are themselves valued by this site below or near their own prices. On four methods the fair value is about **Rs 60.50**. I'd buy at up to **Rs 51.40** and treat under **Rs 45.40** as a strong buy. The business passes 2 of 4 tests (debt, steady profit; it fails returns and cash), so it is **category 3, avoid for now**.

**Valuation table (Rs per share)**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sum of the parts | 53.3 | 82.5 | 118.2 | 80.9 |
| P/E | 42.7 | 53.5 | 67.9 | 53.2 |
| Justified P/B | 45.4 | 58.1 | 76.6 | 58.0 |
| Residual income | 37.3 | 49.8 | 69.0 | 49.9 |
| **Average** | **44.7** | **61.0** | **82.9** | **60.5** |

Weights bear 30 / base 50 / bull 20. Buy price = fair value less 15% (Rs 51.40), strong buy = less 25% (Rs 45.40).

**What the company owns (30 September 2026)**

- LB Finance PLC: 286.73mn shares (51.75% direct; 66.34% with Royal Ceramics' stake). Profit Rs 14.04bn in 2025/26, equity Rs 63.3bn, ROE about 24%. Worth Rs 45.6bn at Rs 159.
- Royal Ceramics Lanka PLC: 620.03mn shares (55.96%). Worth Rs 29.1bn at Rs 47.00 (CSE close, 16 November 2026). This site values it at Rs 27.20 a share (category 3).
- Sampath Bank PLC: 175.35mn shares (14.95%), carried at Rs 24.5bn (Rs 140.00) in September; Rs 26.6bn at Rs 151.75 (CSE close, 16 November). This site values it at Rs 186.
- Unlisted: Delmege (68.75%, cost Rs 2.65bn, Vallibel One's share of profit Rs 1.00bn in 2025/26), Greener Water (100%, cost Rs 7.35bn, hotel completion "further extended"), Swisstek Aluminium (37.56% direct, cost Rs 0.49bn), Vallibel One Properties.
- The Fortress Resorts PLC: 18.59% at March (market value Rs 0.45bn); bought up to 50.74% on 21–22 October 2026 (cost not given in the reports read).
- Holding-company cash and short-term investments Rs 3.99bn, lease liabilities Rs 0.12bn.

**Methods**

*Sum of the parts.* The natural method for a holding company. LB Finance isn't covered by this site, so it's valued on its own book value at a justified price to book (its ROE is about 20–24%, beta 0.97, cost of equity about 18.2%): 0.82x / 1.15x / market. Royal Ceramics and Sampath use this site's own bear/base/bull values, so the views stay consistent. The holding-company discount is 20% / 10% / 0%: the holding company's running costs are covered by the technical fees it charges (admin Rs 0.50bn vs other income Rs 0.49bn in 2025/26), so the discount stands for control (the Perera family and related companies own about 80%; 19.5% is public) and profit kept in the subsidiaries. Result Rs 53.3 / 82.5 / 118.2.

*P/E.* Base EPS Rs 12.20 for 2026/27 (H1 Rs 4.93 + Rs 7.30), level with the Rs 12.47 run-rate. Justified forward P/E at the cost of equity 3.9x / 4.4x / 5.1x. Result Rs 42.7 / 53.5 / 67.9.

*Justified P/B and residual income.* Owners' ROE has been 10–12.5% for three years (18.9% in 2021/22). Long-run ROE 10.5% / 12% / 13.5% against a cost of equity of 19.8% / 18.3% / 16.8% means kept profit earns less than shareholders require, so book value is worth less than its face: 0.41x–0.69x NAV.

*Dividends.* Rs 3.00 a year for two years (Rs 1.00 and nothing in the two years before): a 26% payout and a 3.4% yield. A dividend model (Rs 3.00 growing 4–6% at 16.8–19.8%) gives only Rs 20–29 because three-quarters of profit is kept, so it isn't in the average. The dividend itself is safe: the holding company received Rs 4.14bn of dividends in 2025/26 (Rs 2.22bn in this half) against Rs 3.42bn paid.

*DCF.* Not used. The consolidated cash flow is dominated by LB Finance's lending (loans +Rs 136.6bn last year), so a whole-company DCF would be meaningless; the operating businesses are valued by a DCF inside this site's Royal Ceramics analysis, which feeds the sum of the parts.

**Required return**

Cost of equity = 8.24% + 0.98 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.3% (bear 19.8%, bull 16.8%). Risk-free = 12.24% bond yield − 4.0% default spread. Beta 0.98 (provisional): the value-weighted average of LB Finance 0.97 (finance companies), Royal Ceramics 1.12 (this site's figure), Sampath 0.70 (money-centre banks) and the unlisted operating businesses 1.28; one local 5-year beta found (StockAnalysis 0.87). No WACC: the holding company has no debt, and the group's borrowings are LB Finance's funding.

**Growth check**

Profit kept × ROE = 74.1% × 11.5% = 8.5% supported. The methods assume 4% / 5% / 6% long-run, all below it and below the 12.24% bond yield.

**Business tests (2 of 4)**

- Returns: fail. Owners' ROE 11.5% (2025/26), 10.1%, 12.5%, 14.9%, 18.9% in the years before.
- Debt: pass. The holding company has net cash; the group's Rs 180bn of debt is LB Finance's deposit and bank funding (loans Rs 377bn at September). Royal Ceramics' net debt is 0.55x its equity.
- Steady profit: pass. Owners' profit in each of the last ten years, Rs 9.5–13.2bn over the last five.
- Cash: fail. Only about Rs 4.1bn of the Rs 13.2bn owners' profit reached the holding company as dividends last year; LB Finance's growth absorbs its capital, and Royal Ceramics' operating cash flow is weak.

**Buy plan (500 shares)**

- 200 shares up to Rs 60.50
- 150 shares up to Rs 51.40
- 150 shares up to Rs 45.40

Average about Rs 53.24, total about Rs 26,620 (Rs 44,400 at Rs 88.80). Not realistic soon: the share traded Rs 88.20–104.00 from April to September 2026 and Rs 82–115 over the past year (web range); it was last near Rs 51–58 between March 2024 (Rs 50.50) and mid-2025 (low Rs 56.20 in the June 2025 quarter).

**What would change the view**

Higher: LB Finance keeping ROE above 20% with clean credit; Royal Ceramics' operating businesses earning above 12% on capital; Greener Water's hotel opening or being sold; a lower beta after January's refresh; a higher payout. Lower: credit losses at LB Finance (the Rs 1.9bn receivables impairment this half); a weaker Sampath share price; money put into the Lanka Walltiles rights issue or the Fortress Resorts without a return; another delay at Greener Water.

**Uncertain or missing**

The current CSE price couldn't be fetched (network block) and Rs 88.80 is the 30 September close; the site's daily CSE close will replace it. LB Finance's price (Rs 159) is from a 9 November broker table. LB Finance's share count (554mn) is worked out from the 51.75% stake. The cost of the October Fortress purchase isn't in the reports read. Delmege's book value is unclear (the subsidiary summary and the minority-interest balance don't agree), so it is valued on profit. Group capex booked and working-capital change weren't recorded because the group figures mix LB Finance's lending with the operating businesses.
